item.title: Iran says US proposal narrowed gaps but uranium, toll disputes persist
item.description: Iran indicated on Thursday that the latest American proposal has partially reduced differences between the two sides, even as it prepares a formal response to a plan that would see the Strait of Hormuz reopened and the US naval blockade of Iranian ports lifted. However, a dispute over Iran's push for a permanent toll system in the waterway and Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's reported refusal to surrender Tehran's enriched uranium stockpile threaten to derail progress toward a lasting peace.

item.title: Trump to send 5,000 additional troops to Poland, reversing earlier cuts
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced Thursday that the United States will send an additional 5,000 troops to Poland, a reversal that comes just days after the Pentagon characterized its earlier cancellation of a similar-sized deployment as merely a "temporary delay."

"We will put more there if they want it," Trump said, emphasizing that Washington works "very closely" with Warsaw.

item.title: Rutte says many NATO allies 'not spending enough' on Ukraine
item.description: NATO foreign ministers convened in Helsingborg, Sweden, on Thursday for a two-day meeting focused on sustaining long-term support for Ukraine, with Secretary General Mark Rutte warning that many alliance members are "not spending enough" to help Kyiv defend itself against Russia's full-scale invasion.

item.title: Trump, Rubio reject Iran's plan for Hormuz toll system
item.description: Iran is in active talks with Oman to establish a permanent toll system for ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, formalizing Tehran's control over one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints. The move drew sharp rebukes from both President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Thursday.

item.title: Russia developing seabed nuclear missiles, German investigation finds
item.description:
NATO intelligence services have been closely tracking Russia's Northern Fleet amid growing concerns that Moscow is advancing a secret program to deploy nuclear-armed missiles on the Arctic Ocean seabed, according to an investigation published on May 21 by German public broadcasters WDR and NDR. The report identifies a classified project codenamed "Skif," under which Russia is believed to be developing remote-controlled missile systems housed in sealed containers dropped from submarines to the ocean floor.

The revelation comes as Russia wraps up its largest nuclear exercises in years, a three-day drill running from May 19 through May 21 that mobilized nearly 65,000 troops, over 200 missile launchers, 140 aircraft, 73 surface vessels, and 13 submarines — including eight strategic nuclear submarines.

item.title: Palestinian envoy drops UN vice presidency bid after US threats
item.description: Palestinian Ambassador Riyad Mansour has withdrawn his candidacy for a vice president position at the UN General Assembly following pressure from the Trump administration, the United Nations confirmed on Thursday. Lebanon's ambassador will assume the role in his place.

item.title: NATO allies bewildered by Trump's troop reversal
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Helsingborg, Sweden, on Friday for a NATO foreign ministers' meeting, carrying a message from President Donald Trump about allied shortcomings during the Iran conflict while trying to calm growing European anxiety over Washington's shifting military commitments on the continent.

item.title: Rubio cites 'slight progress' in US-Iran peace talks
item.description:
Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi in Tehran as Islamabad pushed to narrow the remaining gaps between Washington and Tehran in stalled peace negotiations. Speaking at a NATO foreign ministers' meeting in Helsingborg, Sweden, Secretary of State Marco Rubio offered a cautious assessment of the diplomatic efforts.

"There has been some slight progress. I don't want to exaggerate it, but there's been a little bit of movement, and that's good," Rubio told reporters on Friday.

item.title: WHO upgrades Congo Ebola risk to 'very high' as cases surge
item.description:
The World Health Organization on Friday upgraded its risk assessment for the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo from "high" to "very high" at the national level, as the rapidly escalating epidemic now encompasses nearly 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the outbreak is "spreading rapidly" and warned that the actual scale is likely far larger than official figures suggest. There are now 82 confirmed cases in the DRC along with seven confirmed fatalities, but Tedros indicated the true toll could exceed 1,000 infections, with cases significantly underreported for months before detection.

item.title: Iran condemns US sanctions on its envoy to Lebanon
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry on Friday strongly condemned the US Treasury Department's decision to sanction Tehran's designated ambassador to Lebanon, Mohammad Reza Sheibani, calling the move "illegal and unjustified" and accusing Washington of violating international law and the UN Charter.

item.title: 4 dead, 90 trapped in China coal mine after CO buildup
item.description: Four workers have been confirmed dead and 90 remain trapped underground after carbon monoxide levels exceeded safe limits at a coal mine in Changzhi City, in northern China's Shanxi Province, according to a Reuters report citing the state news agency Xinhua.

item.title: SpaceX launches first Starship V3 but loses booster over Gulf of Mexico
item.description:
SpaceX launched its upgraded Starship V3 megarocket on Friday evening from Starbase, Texas, marking the debut of the company's most powerful rocket design yet. While the upper stage successfully deployed 22 dummy Starlink satellites and completed a controlled splashdown in the Indian Ocean, the Super Heavy booster crashed uncontrolled into the Gulf of Mexico after its engines failed to perform as planned.

The flight, which lifted off at 5:33 p.m. CDT from SpaceX's new Pad 2, came one day after a hydraulic pin on the launch tower arm failed to retract, scrubbing the first attempt at T-minus 40 seconds. Upper-level winds pushed the launch from its initial 5:30 p.m. window to 6:30 p.m. CDT on Friday.

item.title: NATO weighs return to Iraq after wartime evacuation
item.description:
NATO's advisory mission to Iraq, which was fully evacuated to southern Italy amid the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, could return to Baghdad in the coming months, the mission's former commander said this week.

French General Christophe Hintzy, who handed command of NATO Mission Iraq to Spanish General Ramon Armada during a change-of-command ceremony this week, told AFP that "the general staff is working on various options" to allow the mission to resume operations inside Iraq.

item.title: Rubio invites Modi to White House amid trade impasse
item.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Saturday, extending a White House invitation on behalf of President Donald Trump as Washington seeks to stabilize a relationship frayed by trade disputes and competing geopolitical pressures.

Rubio's four-day visit — his first official trip to India — comes as the two countries navigate a complicated trade landscape shaped by court rulings that dismantled much of Trump's tariff architecture and new investigations that could reimpose duties on Indian goods.

item.title: US naval blockade of Iran hits 100 redirected ships
item.description:
U.S. Central Command announced on Friday that American forces have redirected more than 100 commercial vessels since the naval blockade of Iranian ports began on April 13, marking a milestone in the six-week-old maritime operation designed to choke off Tehran's oil exports.

The achievement comes as CENTCOM steadily escalated its enforcement figures — from 37 ships redirected by April 25, to 58 by May 8, 67 by May 12, 85 by May 18, and 94 as of May 21 — underscoring the pace of commercial traffic still attempting to reach Iranian waters despite the blockade.

item.title: Ukraine hits Russian frigate, oil terminals in Novorossiysk
item.description: Ukrainian forces launched a multi-target overnight assault on the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiysk on the night of May 22-23, hitting the frigate Admiral Essen, a missile hovercraft, and oil infrastructure, according to Ukrainian military sources and Russian officials.

item.title: Zelensky confirms strike on chemical plant 1,700 km inside Russia
item.description: Ukraine escalated its long-range drone campaign overnight on May 23, hitting an oil terminal in the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk and a chemical plant nearly 1,700 kilometers from the border, as Kyiv continues to target the energy and industrial infrastructure underpinning Russia's war machine.

item.title: U.S. has 'almost completely excluded' Israel from Iran talks, officials say
item.description: The United States has "almost completely excluded" Israel from ongoing negotiations with Iran, Israeli defense officials told The New York Times this week, as a widening rift between President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu threatens to reshape Middle Eastern geopolitics.

item.title: Taiwan says China deployed 100-plus vessels after Trump-Xi summit
item.description: Taiwan's National Security Council chief Joseph Wu said Saturday that China has deployed more than 100 navy, coast guard, and other vessels across regional waters in what marks one of Beijing's largest maritime shows of force in recent memory, raising alarm over China's intentions toward the self-governing island.

item.title: Zelensky calls Germany's associate EU membership plan 'unfair'
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told EU leaders in a letter sent late on Friday that a German proposal to grant Ukraine "associate" membership of the European Union was "unfair" because it would leave Kyiv without a voice inside the bloc, according to Reuters, which reviewed the message.

"It would be unfair for Ukraine to be present in the European Union, but remain voiceless," Zelensky wrote. "The time is right to move forward with Ukraine's membership in a full and meaningful way."
